stages.name: Chapter 1
stages.blurb: Vice Beach, the opening missions — and the balcony meditation window that may close.

stages.name: Chapter 2
stages.blurb: The cartel money starts moving; stranger strands begin to open.

stages.name: Chapter 3
stages.blurb: VCIA, headlines and the mid-game strands.

stages.name: Chapter 4
stages.blurb: The net tightens; choices start to count.

stages.name: Finale
stages.blurb: Chapter 5 and the final mission — finish the story before deep cleanup.

stages.name: Activities & collectibles
stages.blurb: Stunts, ranges, races, cards, spots and strands — the big cleanup stage.

stages.name: Free roam, money & 100%
stages.blurb: Partner crime, laundering, properties and the last percentage points.

trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.guide: The platinum: earn the other 54 trophies and this one is awarded last, on top of the pile.

steps.text: Work the roadmap in order: story first (stages 1–5), then activities and collectibles (stage 6), then money and 100% cleanup (stage 7).
Hold the one missable risk in mind from the first hour: the Chapter 1 balcony meditation for Positive Mental Attitude.
When the other 54 trophies are earned, the platinum unlocks automatically — there is nothing separate to collect.

trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
trophies.guide: Story trophy for Gone Fishing, the opening mission — it cannot be missed.

steps.text: Play through the prologue mission Gone Fishing; the trophy pops on the mission-complete screen.
No choices, collectibles or score targets gate it — a straight clear of the mission is enough.
It doubles as the tutorial for switching between the two leads, which later partner trophies rely on.

trophies.name: Paradise Lost
trophies.guide: Finish Chapter 1 — and meditate on the balcony before the chapter closes behind you.

steps.text: Complete every Chapter 1 story mission in order; the trophy lands on the chapter's end screen.
Before the chapter ends, do the balcony meditation at Jason's place — several guides warn the spot may not be reachable later.

trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
trophies.guide: Finish Chapter 2; a hidden trophy, awarded as the chapter closes.

steps.text: Play the Chapter 2 mission chain through to its finale mission.
Chapter trophies are awarded on the chapter end screen, not per mission — nothing extra to collect on the way.
It is hidden on PSN, so it will not show in your list until it pops.

trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
trophies.guide: Finish Chapter 3, the VCIA chapter.

steps.text: Complete the Chapter 3 mission chain, including the airport storyline.
While the airport is open to you, take the Catch Me If You Can departure — it is far easier now than in free roam.
The trophy is hidden on PSN and pops on the chapter end screen.

trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma
trophies.guide: Finish Chapter 4.

steps.text: Play the Chapter 4 chain to its end; the trophy pops on the chapter end screen.
Chapter 4 is where the choice counter (Actions Speak Louder) starts moving fastest — pick dialogue options rather than skipping scenes.
Hidden on PSN until earned.

trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off
trophies.guide: Finish the final mission — the story's gold closer.

steps.text: Complete the final mission of Chapter 5 to earn the gold.
The trophy is tied to finishing the mission, not to which late-game choices you made on the way.
After the credits you return to free roam on the same save, so all cleanup can continue afterwards.

trophies.name: Trust
trophies.guide: Finish Breakfast Run, an early Chapter 1 mission.

steps.text: Breakfast Run arrives early in Chapter 1; finish it as part of the normal story flow.
It teaches the partner hand-off the later duo trophies (Hot Together, Retail Therapy) are built around.

trophies.name: Break the Bank
trophies.guide: Finish The Cartel Heist, Chapter 2's set-piece mission.

steps.text: Complete The Cartel Heist when it opens in Chapter 2.
Stage a fast car before the escape leg — the getaway is the only part that can fail you.
Hidden on PSN; it pops on the mission-complete screen.

trophies.name: Family Matters
trophies.guide: Finish the mission Child's Play.

steps.text: Child's Play is a Chapter 2 story mission; complete it in the chain.
No optional objectives are required — the trophy is for the clear, not a medal.
Hidden on PSN until it pops.

trophies.name: DWNFALL
trophies.guide: Finish the mission Headliners.

steps.text: Headliners is a Chapter 3 mission; play it as it unlocks in the chain.
The mission's public set-piece draws a crowd — expect a wanted level on the way out, but only the clear matters.
Hidden on PSN until earned.

trophies.name: Hi-Jacked
trophies.guide: Finish VCIA Takedown, the airport mission — and use the airside access while you have it.

steps.text: Complete VCIA Takedown in Chapter 3.
The mission puts you airside at the airport; that access is what Catch Me If You Can needs, so take the departure before you leave.
Hidden on PSN until it pops.

trophies.name: Snow Storm
trophies.guide: Finish Operation Savage Glory, a late-game assault mission.

steps.text: Operation Savage Glory sits late in the story; complete it on the way to the finale.
It is a combat-heavy mission — a good place to work the Gunslinger Combat Focus takedowns.
Hidden on PSN until earned.

trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.guide: Reach 100% completion — story, strands, activities, collectibles and the whole map, all of it.

steps.text: Finish the story first, then work the 100% categories: missions, strangers, activities, collectibles and world exploration.
The stats page tracks your completion percentage by category — use it to find what is missing instead of guessing.
Meditation spots, card sets and WAiNK locations all count toward the total; none of them can be skipped.
The trophy awards the moment the counter reaches 100%, completing the pair with the platinum.

trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
trophies.guide: Land 250 stunts — jumps, wheelies and near-miss chains all feed the same counter.

steps.text: Stunt jumps are scattered across the map; each unique jump counts once when you land it cleanly.
Repeatable moves count too — wheelies, stoppies and near-miss chains all add to the running total on the stats page.
A motorcycle is the easiest farm vehicle for the last stretch; causeway and airport ramps are quiet at night.

trophies.name: Master of None
trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Try each of the nine activity types once — starting is enough, winning is not required.

steps.text: The nine types are races, drone races, the shooting range, fishing, arcade games, bowling, meditation, hunting and stunt events.
You only need to start each type once — this trophy does not ask you to win or finish any of them.
The stats page lists the types you have tried; check it to find the one you have somehow missed.
Most types unlock through the story, so sweep this up in stage 6 once the map is fully open.

trophies.name: The Shootist
trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Gold-medal all 42 Shooting Range challenges — accuracy and speed both count.

steps.text: Ranges unlock as the story opens the map; each range hosts a set of weapon challenges.
Gold is score-based: hits, accuracy and clear time all feed the medal, so replay a challenge until its medal turns gold.
Later challenges use heavier weapons — if a late range is still locked, finish the story first and come back.

trophies.name: Top Fun
trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Win a Top Fun drone race at all 14 locations — first place, not just a finish.

steps.text: Each Top Fun location hosts one drone race, and you must win it — a podium finish does not count.
Scout a course before racing it: gates thread rooftops and masts, and one missed gate costs the run.
Wins are tracked per location on the map, so you can see at a glance which courses are still open.

trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
trophies.guide: Win 20 different races — repeating the same event does not add to the count.

steps.text: Any race type counts — street, off-road, boat and air — as long as each win is a different event.
The map marks races you have already won; hunt the un-marked ones when you go looking for the last few.
Short point-to-point races are the fastest wins if you are topping up the count late.

trophies.name: Baited My Tackle
trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Out-fish Cal in one of his pier challenges — beat his weight before the clock runs out.

steps.text: Cal's fishing challenges appear at piers and marinas once fishing is unlocked.
Beat his target weight before the timer ends; casting near structure with heavier bait draws the bigger fish.
Losing costs nothing — you can challenge him again straight away.

trophies.name: Stick Fiddler
trophies.guide: Finish any one arcade game, all the way to its own end screen.

steps.text: Arcade cabinets sit in bars and diners around the state; the retro racer is the shortest game to clear.
You must reach the game's end screen — a high score alone does not complete it.
One finished game is all the trophy asks for; the rest of the cabinets are optional.

trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Finish Andy's whole stranger strand, through to his final mission.

steps.text: Andy's strand opens in Chapter 3; work each of his missions as their icons appear.
A strand only counts when its final mission is done — the trophy pops on that mission's complete screen.
Hidden on PSN until earned.

trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.guide: Finish Kenton's stranger strand and its final mission on the water.

steps.text: Kenton's strand opens around Chapter 3; complete each mission as it surfaces.
The trophy is awarded for the strand's final mission, not the earlier ones.
Hidden on PSN until it pops.

trophies.name: The Lone Rider
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.guide: Finish Billy's stranger strand, ending with his final ride.

steps.text: Billy's strand opens in Chapter 4; follow his icons as they appear.
Complete the strand's final mission — that clear is what the trophy checks.
Hidden on PSN until earned.

trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks
trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.disagree_note: Guides agree that 8 completed strands are required, but they count the pool differently: most list 9 strands across the state, while one counts only the 8 that open before the finale. Either way, finishing any 8 full strands earns it — the disagreement only matters if you are hunting a specific ninth.
trophies.guide: Complete any 8 full stranger strands — starting a strand is not enough, its final mission must be done.

steps.text: A strand is a stranger's whole mission chain; the count only moves when a strand's final mission is complete.
The Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy and Tyrone strands all count toward the eight.
Strand icons appear as you explore new districts; if one stops appearing, progress the story and check back.
Each finished strand also pays out its own trophy (Andy's is Road to Rehabilitation), so the eight overlap with five other bronzes.

trophies.name: Supply & Demand
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide: Finish Randy's stranger strand and its final delivery mission.

steps.text: Randy's strand opens in Chapter 4; run his missions as the icons appear.
The trophy checks the strand's final mission, not the deliveries before it.
Hidden on PSN until it pops.

trophies.name: Spin On This!
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.guide: Finish Tyrone's stranger strand — the earliest strand you can complete.

steps.text: Tyrone's strand opens in Chapter 2, earlier than the other strangers.
Finish the strand's final mission to earn the trophy.
Hidden on PSN until earned.

trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude
trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.missable_note: The Chapter 1 balcony spot may become unreachable when Chapter 1 ends. Meditate there before you finish the chapter — every guide that flags a missable in this game flags this one.
trophies.disagree_note: Two versions circulate. Most guides list 18 meditation spots, and PlayStation's own tracker counts to 18. One 100%-checklist source lists only 15, treating 3 spots as optional. Both versions are shown here — the safe play is to do all 18 and trust your counter. Guides also disagree on whether the Chapter 1 balcony spot stays reachable after Chapter 1; this guide treats it as missable.
trophies.guide: Meditate at every spot in Leonida — and do the Chapter 1 balcony spot before the chapter ends.

steps.text: In Chapter 1, meditate on the balcony at Jason's place before finishing the chapter; several guides warn the spot may be unreachable afterwards.
Spots are marked by small stone cairns at viewpoints; interact and stay for the full animation — leaving early does not register the spot.
The remaining spots spread across beaches, rooftops and the Keys; none besides the balcony is tied to a story window.
Your counter is the authority: PlayStation tracks 18 spots even though one 100% list names only 15 — a stall at 15 means three spots are still out there.
The rest can be finished in free roam after the story; only the balcony spot has a deadline.

trophies.name: Fair Game
trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Complete Bret's hunt for the unique animal that stalks his territory.

steps.text: Bret's hunting strand starts at his camp; the unique animal only appears after his earlier hunts are done.
The unique animal works one fixed territory at dawn — track it from the marked search area rather than roaming.
A clean kill is not required; the trophy is for completing the hunt.

trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck
trophies.guide: Complete any 3 full Collectible Card sets — every card in the set, not just most of it.

steps.text: Cards hide singly and in small caches; a set completes only when every card in it has been found.
Sets are themed by district, so sweeping one district at a time finishes sets fastest.
The collection page shows which cards in a set are still missing — use it before a long hunt.
Any 3 sets count; pick the shortest sets first if you only want the trophy.

trophies.name: You WAiNKer!
trophies.guide: Take the WAiNK photo at 100 marked viewpoints across the state.

steps.text: WAiNK spots are viewpoints where the app prompts you for a photo — the photo must actually be taken, not just the spot visited.
Spots only appear on the map when you are close, so sweep district by district rather than hunting from the full map.
Some spots want a specific time of day; the app tells you when the light is wrong, so come back rather than forcing it.

trophies.name: One Last Thing
trophies.guide: Complete any 50 of the game's scored Challenges.

steps.text: Challenges are the short scored tasks — driving, combat, exploration — listed on the challenges page.
Any 50 count, so play to your strengths and skip the types you dislike.
Story missions unlock many challenges, so finish the story before grinding the last few.

trophies.name: Hot Together
trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: As a duo: earn 4 stars together, then lose them together and escape.

steps.text: Both leads must be together in free roam — start as a duo, not solo.
Raise the wanted level to 4 stars with public crimes, then break line of sight and stay hidden until the stars clear.
Switching character mid-escape cancels the attempt — stay as the pair for the whole run.
A vehicle change out of sight speeds the escape; the trophy pops when the heat fully clears.

trophies.name: Retail Therapy
trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: Chain three shop robberies with your partner while the wanted level never fully clears.

steps.text: Plan a route of three shops close together first — the chain breaks if the wanted level drops to zero.
One partner robs while the other holds the door; the register timer keeps running during the getaway.
Keep pressure on between shops with minor crimes so the stars never lapse mid-chain.

trophies.name: Whip It Good
trophies.guide: Discover 100 different vehicles — you must get in and drive them, not just see them.

steps.text: A vehicle is discovered the first time you drive it; a parked sighting does not count.
Airports, marinas and wealthy districts hold the rare models, and story missions hand you several exotics for free.
The stats page lists vehicle classes you have not discovered yet — use it to aim the last stretch.

trophies.name: Gunslinger
trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Drop 5 enemies inside one Combat Focus activation, before the meter empties.

steps.text: Combat Focus slows time; all five takedowns must land before the meter runs out.
Gang hideouts and the late story set-pieces give the densest groups — line the group up before you trigger it.
Shotguns and explosives register multi-kills fastest, but takedowns from any weapon count.
A full meter gives the longest window; top it up before you make the attempt.

trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can
trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.missable_note: Easiest during the Chapter 3 VCIA Takedown mission, while you are already airside. It stays possible in free roam, but the route back airside is much longer — do it during the mission.
trophies.guide: Leave Vice City International Airport through a gap that is not a gate, while you are airside.

steps.text: The clean chance comes during VCIA Takedown, when the mission puts you airside at the airport.
Drive out through the service gap by the cargo ramps instead of the marked exit; the trophy pops as you clear the fence line.
Missed it? Airside access returns in free roam via the staff car park — slower, but the trophy is never fully lost.

trophies.name: Challenging Tank
trophies.guide: Survive a Rhino tank encounter — the exact trigger is still only partly documented.

steps.text: Rhinos roll out at the highest wanted levels and during the finale's armoured push.
The reported trigger is to draw a Rhino's attention and escape its patrol zone alive — treat any tank encounter as a chance and survive it.
Only one guide documents this trophy so far, and the trigger is unconfirmed; if it does not pop on an escape, try surviving a full shelling before you break away.

trophies.name: Sneakthief
trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: Empty a jewelry store without the detection meter ever filling — in and out unseen.

steps.text: Case the store first: the cameras and the silent alarm decide the attempt, not the guards.
Disable the alarm panel before you take the cases, and watch the camera sweep while you work.
Being spotted after the loot is bagged still voids it — the escape has to stay clean too.

trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal
trophies.guide: Crack 5 bank vaults and escape after each one — a breach without an escape does not count.

steps.text: Vault jobs open once robbery prep is available; each bank offers its vault on a cooldown after a hit.
A vault only counts when you escape and lose the wanted level with the take.
Rotate across districts — five different branches is the cleanest route to five.
Stage the getaway car before you start the drill; vault escapes start at high heat.

trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play
trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Hit an armored truck, breach it, and escape with the money.

steps.text: Armored trucks run fixed routes; ambush one away from police patrols.
The rear doors need explosives or the cutter — set the breach up before you block the truck.
The trophy needs the escape, not just the breach: lose the wanted level with the money aboard.

trophies.name: The Goodtime State
trophies.disagree_note: PlayStation's tracker counts 52 areas. One guide's region list names only 50, folding two late-unlocked island areas into their neighbours. The in-game counter is the authority: if you are stuck at 50, the two Keys areas are the usual misses.
trophies.guide: Reveal the whole map — all 52 tracked areas of Leonida.

steps.text: An area counts when you enter it and its name card appears; skimming the border road is not always enough.
The islands and the far Keys are the common misses — a boat sweep of the coast finishes the set.
Two areas unlock only late in the story, so sitting at 50 of 52 before the finale is normal, not a bug.

trophies.name: Pest Control
trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Rob one Illegal Operation for each of the nine gangs.

steps.text: Each gang's operation is marked once you discover it — and the robbery, not the visit, is what counts.
The map's gang overlay shows which gangs you have already hit.
The last gangs only surface their operations once the story reaches their territory.
Operations respawn, so a failed robbery costs time, not the trophy.

trophies.name: In The Beginning…
trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.missable_note: The Ocean Beach terrace is there all game, but the story frames this moment in Chapter 1 — guides suggest taking the seat while Chapter 1 keeps you on Ocean Beach, exactly as the game opens.
trophies.guide: Take the cocktail and the seat with the view at Ocean Beach, just like the opening frames it.

steps.text: At the Ocean Beach terrace bar, order a cocktail and take the marked seat facing the water.
Stay seated until the short scene finishes — standing up early cancels the moment.
It costs a few dollars and two minutes; do it in Chapter 1 and it is one less thing to remember.

trophies.name: Capital Offense
trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: Steal a display car and drive it straight out through the showroom glass.

steps.text: The downtown showroom keeps display cars beside the glass frontage; take one and aim it at the glass.
Any showroom car works — the trophy is for the exit, not the model.
You will leave with a wanted level; the trophy pops on the way out, before any escape.

trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling
trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: Bowl at the Kolt & Associates alley and land the follow-through on the final frame.

steps.text: The alley is a playable activity — start a game and bowl your frames.
The follow-through is the lane's trick-shot prompt on the last frame; hitting it completes the moment the trophy names.
A lost game still counts — only the follow-through matters.

trophies.name: Personal Best
trophies.guide: A two-lead moment the guides have only partly pinned down — watch for it in the late game.

steps.text: The description points at a partnership moment; the reported trigger is a character switch at a viewpoint with both leads together.
If it does not pop in free roam, the fallback report ties it to a story partnership beat in the finale — do not skip the finale's duo scenes.
Listed as unconfirmed: only one source documents it so far, so this guide shows the report rather than a promise.

trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder
trophies.disagree_note: PlayStation's tracker counts choices up to 500, yet several guides report the trophy arriving much earlier, at a fixed story choice in Chapter 4. Both versions are shown: if it has not popped by the finale, keep making dialogue and world choices in free roam — the tracker keeps counting either way.
trophies.guide: Make choices — dialogue picks, mercy calls, world interactions — they all feed one counter.

steps.text: Every dialogue option and either/or world interaction adds to the choice counter.
Story choices alone will not reach the cap; free-roam interactions — help, rob, greet, spare — count too.
If you are grinding the tail, the stats page shows the running count.

trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess
trophies.guide: Fail at something, then succeed at the same thing on the second try.

steps.text: The reported pattern is a failed attempt followed by a successful retry of the same event — a race, a challenge or a robbery.
Guides could not isolate exactly which events qualify, so simply retry anything you fail and it should land quickly.
Unconfirmed in detail and single-source for now — this guide shows the report as a report.

trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There
trophies.guide: Witness one of Leonida's strange free-roam events — you only have to see it start.

steps.text: Strange events are rare free-roam encounters: lights over the swamp, a figure on the causeway at night.
The Glades at night is the most-reported location — linger there rather than driving through.
You only need to witness the event begin; no interaction is required.

trophies.name: Ten Pin
trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: Knock a pedestrian down with a melee swing from a moving vehicle.

steps.text: Ride as a passenger or on a bike and swing a melee weapon while passing a pedestrian at speed.
The hit must connect while the vehicle is moving — a stationary swing does not count.
Slow passes along a busy sidewalk give the cleanest angle.

trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar
trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Launder $250,000 of Marked Bills through your contacts — the laundered total is what counts.

steps.text: Marked Bills come from vault and armored-truck robberies; hand them to a laundering contact instead of spending them raw.
The counter tracks the laundered figure, not the size of the take — bank every score, even small ones.
The stats page shows your running laundered total.

trophies.name: Treat Yo Self
trophies.guide: Spend $100,000 across all shops — cumulative, over the whole game.

steps.text: Every shop counts — clothes, weapons, vehicles, services — and the total accumulates across the whole playthrough.
Property purchases do not count here; that money belongs to Little Boxes. This is shop tills only.
Most players pass the total naturally during 100% cleanup; if you are short, vehicle purchases close the gap fastest.

trophies.name: Little Boxes
trophies.guide: Buy all 8 garage properties — the last one only lists after the finale.

steps.text: Garages come up for sale as the story opens districts; the property icon shows the asking price.
You need the cash up front — laundering income (Dime on the Dollar) is the natural way to fund the late purchases.
The eighth garage lists only after the finale, so this is an endgame buy by design.

trophies.name: On the Spot
trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app — story-gifted cars count.

steps.text: Any vehicle you own can be registered at a garage or through the phone app once it is stored.
Vehicles the story gives you count — register them as they arrive instead of buying ten.
Registration is free; the trophy is about using the system, not about spending.
